rule_metadata.description: The definitive, centralized module for Madd Lazim, covering all four sub-categories (Kalimi Thaqil, Kalimi Khafif, Harfi Thaqil, and Harfi Khafif) anchored by a mandatory 6-count duration.

theoretical_foundation.linguistic_definition: Lazim (لَازِم) means compulsory, mandatory, or permanent.
theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: Madd Lazim occurs when a Madd letter is followed by a permanent Sukoon or a Shaddah (representing a doubled consonant) within the same word or inside the disjointed letters (Al-Huroof al-Muqatta'ah) at the start of Surahs.
theoretical_foundation.ruling_and_duration: Strictly and universally extended for exactly **6 counts** (Harakat) across all authentic transmission paths.

the_four_sub_categories.kalimi_thaqil: 1. Madd Lazim Kalimi Thaqil (Word-Based Heavy): A Madd letter followed by a Shaddah in the same word (e.g., الضَّالِّينَ, الحَاقَّةُ).
the_four_sub_categories.kalimi_khafif: 2. Madd Lazim Kalimi Khafif (Word-Based Light): A Madd letter followed by a permanent unmerged Sukoon in a word. Found in only one word in the entire Quran, appearing twice: آلْآنَ (Surah Yunus).
the_four_sub_categories.harfi_thaqil: 3. Madd Lazim Harfi Thaqil (Letter-Based Heavy): Found in isolated letters at Surah openings whose spelled-out ending letter merges into the succeeding letter (e.g., the Meem in المٓ merging into the Lam or Meem).
the_four_sub_categories.harfi_khafif: 4. Madd Lazim Harfi Khafif (Letter-Based Light): Found in isolated letters at Surah openings whose spelled-out ending letter is followed by a non-merging Sukoon (e.g., the Qaf in قٓ or Noon in نٓ).

theoretical_foundation.mushaf_indicator: A wavy Maddah sign (~) placed over the Madd letter, followed by a Shaddah or clear Sukoon.

practical_examples.breakdown: Alif Madd followed by a Shaddah on the Lam inside the same word; extended strictly for 6 counts.
Alif Madd followed by permanent unmerged Sukoon in Surah Yunus; 6 counts.
Laam ends in Meem merging into succeeding Meem (Thaqil 6 counts); Meem ends in Saakin Mim (Khafif 6 counts).

assessment_bank.question: What does 'Lazim' mean linguistically?
What is the universal duration required for all forms of Madd Lazim?
What are the two primary structural domains where Madd Lazim occurs?
options: Within words (Kalimi) and within disjointed opening letters (Harfi)

assessment_bank.question: What distinguishes Thaqil (Heavy) from Khafif (Light) in Madd Lazim?
options: Thaqil has a succeeding Shaddah (doubled consonant/merging), whereas Khafif has a clear unmerged Sukoon

assessment_bank.question: In the word 'الضَّالِّينَ', what specific sub-category of Madd Lazim applies?
Where does Madd Lazim Kalimi Khafif occur in the Quran?
options: In only one word appearing twice: آلْآنَ in Surah Yunus

assessment_bank.question: In the opening letters 'المٓ', how is the letter 'Laam' (لَام) classified?
options: Madd Lazim Harfi Thaqil (because its spelled-out ending 'Meem' merges into the succeeding 'Meem' of 'Meem')

assessment_bank.question: In 'قٓ ۚ وَالْقُرْآنِ', how is the letter 'Qaf' (قَاف) classified?
options: Madd Lazim Harfi Khafif (because its spelled-out ending 'Fa' has no succeeding letter to merge into)

assessment_bank.question: What happens if a reciter reads Madd Lazim with only 2 counts?
options: It is a major Tajweed violation (Lahn Jali) because 6 counts are mandatory

assessment_bank.question: What Mushaf symbol signals Madd Lazim across its variants?
Why is Madd Lazim ranked at the very top of Aqwa al-Mudud (the hierarchy of Madd strength)?
options: Because its cause (permanent Sukoon/Shaddah) is absolute and unalterable
Because it is the shortest rule

assessment_bank.question: In 'الْحَاقَّةُ', what rule governs the Alif followed by a doubled Qaf?
Which disjointed opening letter (Al-Huroof al-Muqatta'ah) has NO Madd at all?
Why does 'Alif' (أَلِفْ) have no Madd Lazim?
options: Because its spelled-out three-letter name (أ - ل - ف) contains no central Madd letter in its middle position
Because it is at the end of an ayah

assessment_bank.question: What is the exact counting rhythm for a 6-count Madd Lazim execution?
options: A steady, unhurried pulse holding vocal extension across 6 finger movements

assessment_bank.question: In 'طٰهٰ', how are Ta and Ha lengthened?
options: 2 counts each (Madd Tabii Harfi, NOT Lazim because their spelling names lack 3 letters with central Madd)

assessment_bank.question: In 'كهيعص', which letters receive the full 6-count Madd Lazim?
How does an AI evaluation engine grade a student who recites 'الضَّالِّينَ' with 6 counts?
options: Mark as perfect and fully compliant with Madd Lazim Kalimi Thaqil standards

assessment_bank.question: What is the acoustic effect of Madd Lazim Kalimi Thaqil?
options: A majestic 6-count elongation crashing into a heavy, doubled consonant sound with Shaddah

assessment_bank.question: Can Madd Lazim occur across two separate words?
options: No, Lazim strictly occurs within a single word or single isolated letter name

assessment_bank.question: What is the purpose of unifying all Madd Lazim variants into Module 02?
options: To provide a centralized, comprehensive master home for all word-based and letter-based compulsory rules

assessment_bank.question: In 'حَٓمْ ۝ عَسَقْ', what rule governs the spelled-out ending letters like 'Meem' and 'Seen'?
What is the structural definition of Kalimi in Madd Lazim?
options: Pertaining to standard dictionary words (Kalimah) rather than isolated letters

assessment_bank.question: What is the structural definition of Harfi in Madd Lazim?
options: Pertaining to the isolated letters of the alphabet found at Surah openings

assessment_bank.question: In 'آلْآنَ', why is it classified as Kalimi Khafif?
options: Because the Alif Madd is followed by a clear, unmerged Sukoon on the Lam inside a word

assessment_bank.question: If a student confuses Madd Lazim with Madd Muttasil, what is the core correction?
options: Muttasil is 4-5 counts triggered by Hamzah; Lazim is strictly 6 counts triggered by permanent Sukoon/Shaddah

assessment_bank.question: What mnemonic device helps students remember the 8 letters of Harfi Madd Lazim ('كم عسل نقص')?
options: The classic scholarly grouping containing Kaaf, Meem, Ayn, Seen, Lam, Noon, Qaf, Saad

assessment_bank.question: How many counts are required for the 'Ain' (ع) in 'كهيعص' or 'عسق'?
options: 4 or 6 counts (permissible scholarly variance, with 6 being preferred)

assessment_bank.question: What is the role of the permanent Sukoon in Madd Lazim?
options: It serves as the definitive structural trigger that forces the 6-count mandatory elongation

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the unified Madd Lazim rule in one master statement:
options: Any Madd letter followed by a permanent Sukoon or Shaddah—whether inside a word (Kalimi) or an opening letter name (Harfi)—must be rigidly extended for exactly 6 counts across all four sub-categories

assessment_bank.question: In 'صَآفَّاتٍ', what rule applies to the Alif followed by a Shaddah?
In 'طָّسْمۤ', how is the transition executed?
options: Meem merges into Noon or similar rules with Harfi Lazim 6 counts

assessment_bank.question: What is the penalty for shortening Madd Lazim in professional Quranic recitation certification (Ijazah)?
options: Considered a severe recitation flaw violating foundational rules

assessment_bank.question: In 'الضَّالِّينَ', what exact letter carries the Shaddah?
Does Madd Lazim change its count depending on recitation speed (Hadr vs Tartil)?
options: The ratio remains a stable 6 counts relative to the overall tempo
It drops to 2 counts in fast reading

assessment_bank.question: What is the relationship between Madd Lazim and Mushaf orthography?
options: Explicitly marked with a bold Maddah sign (~) across all authoritative Mushafs

assessment_bank.question: If a student asks whether Harfi Lazim applies to all letters of the Arabic alphabet, what is the answer?
options: No, it applies exclusively to the specific isolated letters at Surah openings whose spelled-out names contain a central Madd letter

assessment_bank.question: In 'المٓ', how many total 6-count Madd Lazim segments are performed?
options: Two (Laam ending in Meem = Thaqil 6 counts; Meem ending in Sukoon = Khafif 6 counts)

assessment_bank.question: How should an AI scoring engine evaluate a 6-count recitation of 'آلْآنَ'?
options: Mark as precise Madd Lazim Kalimi Khafif compliance

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the complete unified Madd Lazim module structure:
options: A centralized master module covering Kalimi Thaqil, Kalimi Khafif, Harfi Thaqil, and Harfi Khafif under the mandatory 6-count rule
